title: Duality preserves the disjointness event
statement: Let $\omega$ be a sample of the hard distribution, and let $\omega^\ast$ be its dual, obtained by exchanging Alice's and Bob's roles while reversing the order of the coordinates. Then Alice's and Bob's input sets $X(\omega^\ast)$ and $Y(\omega^\ast)$ are disjoint if and only if $X(\omega)$ and $Y(\omega)$ are disjoint; that is, $\omega^\ast$ lies in the disjointness event exactly when $\omega$ does.
